A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoE-versus-dense study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 4–7 and Appendix E report original architecture ablations, pretraining results, data-reuse experiments, and downstream evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original training and evaluation results, including model comparisons, architecture ablations, and downstream benchmark accuracies.

M1.justification: The architecture-selection framework, routing choices, activation-rate optimization, and strict/loose data-reuse procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A explicitly describes the auxiliary loss as used throughout the experiments; its added formulas document an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining coverage and downstream benchmark suite listed in Appendix D. The new corpus-source breakdown in Appendix C documents the existing training mixture rather than establishing additional datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The same dense baselines and MoE configurations participate in the corresponding comparisons, including the higher-compute dense baselines. V2's LLaMA-1 comparison in Table 3 concerns data recipes, not an additional evaluated model.

E3.justification: Matched experimental tables retain the same model configurations, token and compute budgets, hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics. Section 3.4 newly describes dense-baseline tuning, but the resulting configurations and scores already appear in v1; this does not establish a changed protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: The layer-arrangement, shared-expert, gate-normalization, top-K, model-shape, and data-reuse analyses are retained. V2 expands discussion of existing evidence without adding or removing ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports replicated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the results. V2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 120 experimental rows in matched Appendix E tables and all 48 benchmark accuracy entries in Table 2 retain their values; Figures 1–5 retain their results. For example, optimal 7B BPC remains 0.4543 with unique data, 0.4549 with loose reuse, and 0.4590 with strict reuse.

T1.justification: Appendix A newly supplies mathematical definitions of minibatch expert-selection frequencies, mean gate probabilities, and the auxiliary and total losses in Equations 16–18. The main parameter/compute derivations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that optimized MoEs can surpass dense models under matched resources, identify an approximately 20% optimal activation rate across studied sizes, and use data reuse to address additional token demand. The more assertive title does not change these already-established headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces broad language about reuse benefits with a more qualified interpretation: two-epoch reuse can help at suboptimal activation rates but does not outperform unique data at the optimal 7B point, and further repetition is harmful. It also removes the hypothesis that additional epochs improve router decisions.

D1.justification: V1 describes the internal corpus generically and promises a future model release. V2 provides source-level mixture proportions in Appendix C/Table 3, reports public checkpoint availability with an access link, and documents existing routing/loss and dense-baseline-tuning details. Together these substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix B expand positioning against the already-cited scaling-law studies, emphasizing training sufficiency, fixed parameter budgets, and deployment memory constraints. The cited works are retained; publication-year and venue updates do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted language revisions, expands the reuse and related-work discussions, consolidates notation in the main text, and adds a short LLM-writing-assistance disclosure. Title, author, and publication information change, while the main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICLR title/header layout, consolidates notation into Table 1, adds the data-recipe Table 3, swaps the numbering/order of the dense-baseline and 7B strict-reuse tables, and clarifies highlighted-row captions. Existing scientific figures and result-table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through the corpus recipe and documented checkpoint access, and interprets reuse benefits more cautiously in light of the unchanged results. These gains are tempered by a new inconsistency: Appendix B says dense baselines satisfy D/N ≥ 20, while Table 13 includes values of 19.03 and 10.49.
